assessments.summary: The paired binary-output-table argument establishes the unconditional bound C_out >= 31 c_in^2/(20 ln 2), including the boundary cases. The declared reference establishes that any finite two-letter Marton law exceeding twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value has C_out < 7/160. Combining the bounds gives |c_in| < sqrt(7 ln 2/248) < 7/50. This remains only a necessary condition and does not construct or exclude a Marton gain, prove tensorization, or yield a capacity converse.
scopeQualifications: The reference is required only for the Marton-gain implication C_out < 7/160; the curvature inequality is proved within the subject.
The conclusion applies to finite two-letter Marton laws whose unnormalized value exceeds twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value.
The result is solely a necessary covariance condition; it neither constructs nor rules out a gain, tensorizes Marton's functional, nor proves a capacity converse.
